decisions.reason: The lesson-value standard does not change which source material may be used. The separate one-video source constraint from message 84 is already represented.
Teaching a lesson and capturing a complete beginning-to-end moment are independent clip criteria. The completeness clause from message 84 is already represented.
Requiring a substantive lesson does not necessarily alter the existing hook-selection criterion, and message 84 states no hook change.
The lesson-value standard does not change the existing 20–120 second duration limits.
Moment substance and visual editing style are independent criteria. Message 84's separate visual-style changes are already represented under this candidate.
The substantive-moment criterion does not change the eight-clip batch obligation, which was already current before message 84.
The requirement that moments teach a lesson does not modify caption color treatment.
The substantive-moment criterion does not establish or change any caption-font requirement.
The lesson-value standard does not change the existing target of 180 approved clips per month; message 84 merely repeats that target.
